The supplied Manual practice distinguishes two situations (TMM/Part21/2/2/3):

• If the existing description is broad, vague or absent, an amendment expressly including the words already shown may be appropriate. The description should make clear that the combination of shape or colour and the additional elements is being claimed, not the elements independently. Such a change does not necessarily extend your rights, but requires careful consideration.

• If the existing description already clearly defines the scope of the trade mark, the Manual says the claim cannot be extended to include items outside that description. Words appearing in the representation therefore do not, by themselves, establish that they can be added to the claim.

These are statements of Manual practice, not legislation. No Act or Regulations passages were supplied."}
